title: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea
decision_rule: Covered if every applicable criterion for the order is met. Denied if any is not met. Otherwise insufficient information.

E0470.description: Bi-level respiratory assist device without back-up rate

E0471.description: Bi-level respiratory assist device with back-up rate

criteria.policy_ref: Initial Coverage (implied by 'for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea')
criteria.policy_text: In this policy, the term PAP (positive airway pressure) device will refer to both a single-level continuous positive airway pressure device (E0601) and a bi-level respiratory assist device without back-up rate (E0470) when it is used in the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea.
criteria.check: The record has a diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea.
criteria.notes: Not lettered in the policy, but every other criterion assumes it. A patient with a non-OSA diagnosis (e.g. COPD, hypoventilation) falls under the Respiratory Assist Devices LCD (L33800) instead.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has an in-person clinical evaluation by the treating practitioner prior to the sleep test to assess the beneficiary for obstructive sleep apnea.
criteria.check: An in-person visit with the treating practitioner, assessing for OSA, dated before the sleep test.
evidence: Procedure or note: sleep apnea assessment during that visit
criteria.notes: Timing matters: a visit after the sleep test does not count. For E0470 after a failed E0601 trial, the original evaluation still counts, but if the E0601 was used for more than 3 months a new in-person evaluation is required (Initial Coverage, paragraphs after II).

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has a sleep test (as defined below) that meets either of the following criteria (1 or 2): 1. The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) or Respiratory Disturbance Index (RDI) is greater than or equal to 15 events per hour with a minimum of 30 events; or, 2. The AHI or RDI is greater than or equal to 5 and less than or equal to 14 events per hour with a minimum of 10 events and documentation of: [B2_symptoms]
criteria.check: A sleep test (Type I-IV or other home sleep test) with AHI or RDI >= 15 and at least 30 events, or AHI or RDI 5-14 and at least 10 events.
evidence: DiagnosticReport: sleep study, with test type
criteria.notes: AHI below 5 is not met. AHI 5-14 is met only if B2_symptoms is also met. The event minimums matter mainly for short recordings: if the AHI or RDI is based on less than 2 hours, the events must still reach 30 (or 10 with symptoms) (Definitions). AHI and RDI exclude RERAs.

criteria.applies_when: Only when the AHI or RDI is 5-14. Not applicable when it is >= 15.
criteria.policy_text: a. Excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorders, or insomnia; or, b. Hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke.
criteria.check: Documentation of at least one of: excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, a mood disorder, insomnia, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or a history of stroke.
evidence: Condition: hypertension, ischemic heart disease, stroke, insomnia, mood disorder, or cognitive impairment
Observation: Epworth Sleepiness Scale score, or a note documenting daytime sleepiness
criteria.notes: Any one item from list a or b is enough.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test is ordered by the beneficiary's treating practitioner; and,
criteria.check: The sleep test was ordered by the patient's treating practitioner.
criteria.notes: One of five sleep test requirements under Sleep Tests. Item 3 duplicates criterion B; items 1, 2 and 5 are listed under out_of_scope.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary and/or their caregiver has received instruction from the supplier of the device in the proper use and care of the equipment.
criteria.check: The patient or caregiver received instruction from the device supplier on how to use and care for the device.
evidence: Procedure or DocumentReference: device education or training
criteria.notes: This is supplier documentation and is often absent from clinical records, so 'insufficient information' will be a common correct answer.

criteria.policy_text: An E0601 has been tried and proven ineffective based on a therapeutic trial conducted in either a facility or in a home setting. Ineffective is defined as documented failure to meet therapeutic goals using an E0601 during the titration portion of a facility-based study or during home use despite optimal therapy (i.e., proper mask selection and fitting and appropriate pressure settings).
criteria.check: A CPAP (E0601) trial, in a facility titration or at home, is documented as failing to meet therapeutic goals despite proper mask fit and pressure settings.
evidence: Device or Procedure: CPAP trial or titration study
Observation or note: failure to meet therapeutic goals
Note: mask fitting and pressure settings were optimized
criteria.notes: E0470 only. Simply having used a CPAP is not enough; the record must show it failed despite optimal therapy. This is the cross-document dependency the project highlights: E0470 depends on an E0601 history.

criteria.policy_text: A bi-level positive airway pressure device with back-up rate (E0471) is not reasonable and necessary if the primary diagnosis is OSA. If an E0471 is billed with a diagnosis of OSA, it will be denied as not reasonable and necessary.
criteria.check: An E0471 is not covered when the primary diagnosis is OSA.
criteria.notes: 'not met' if the primary diagnosis is OSA. If it is something else, the Respiratory Assist Devices LCD (L33800) governs instead.

continued_coverage.description: Criteria for keeping a PAP device beyond the first 3 months. Applies to a different kind of case than the initial order, so it is kept separate.
continued_coverage.policy_ref: Continued Coverage Beyond the First Three Months of Therapy

criteria.policy_text: In-person clinical re-evaluation by the treating practitioner with documentation that symptoms of obstructive sleep apnea are improved
criteria.check: An in-person re-evaluation between day 31 and day 91 after starting therapy, documenting improved OSA symptoms.
evidence: Encounter: in-person visit 31-91 days after the device start date
criteria.notes: A re-evaluation after day 91 still qualifies, but coverage restarts from that visit's date.

criteria.policy_text: Objective evidence of adherence to use of the PAP device, reviewed by the treating practitioner. Adherence to therapy is defined as use of PAP >= 4 hours per night on 70% of nights during a consecutive thirty (30) day period anytime during the first three (3) months of initial usage.
criteria.check: Device usage data showing >= 4 hours per night on at least 70% of nights (21 of 30) in some consecutive 30-day period within the first 3 months, reviewed by the treating practitioner.
evidence: Observation: nightly usage hours or a download summary

out_of_scope.reason: Whether the sleep test meets NCD 240.4.1, uses an FDA-approved device, and was run by a qualified Medicare provider are administrative facts not found in a clinical record.

out_of_scope.policy_ref: Re-qualifying after a failed 12 week trial; Replacement; Beneficiaries Entering Medicare; Accessories; Refill Requirements
out_of_scope.reason: Separate claim scenarios. Can be added later as their own checklists if test cases need them.

out_of_scope.policy_ref: Concurrent Use of Oxygen with PAP Therapy
out_of_scope.reason: Requires the Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment LCD (L33797) as well; a good candidate for a later cross-document test case.
